subject: RFI: Performance flighting scenarios and throughput validation
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@novacorp.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: performance details needed for inference platform evaluation

Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking this RFI. Novacorp is evaluating inference vendors for our conversational search product. The procurement team and engineering leads asked for more detailed flighting and validation scenarios before shortlisting. Specifically we need:

- End-to-end latency at p50/p95/p99 for: short chat (avg 40 tokens response), long-context chat (avg 800 tokens response), and embeddings batch (1000 inputs batch).
- Throughput numbers (tokens/sec and requests/sec) for a single 8x A100-equivalent dedicated pool and for a 2-node redundant cluster.
- Test methodology: traffic shapes, synthetic vs replayed traces, cold/warm cache distinction, and sequence-length distribution you used.
- Scaling behavior: how latency degrades with QPS, and what autoscaling/queueing strategies are applied.
- Any constraints / recommended batch sizes / quantization tradeoffs we should be aware of.

Can you provide a concise RFI response and, if helpful, a small workshop to align on test harness and shared datasets? We are targeting a vendor decision by end of July.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Alex
Lead Platform Engineer
Novacorp

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely provide the metrics and a short workshop. High level: Redwood runs benchmark suites in two modes — 1) synthetic step-loads driven by our workload generator (we share the scripts), and 2) replayed production traces from similar customers (anonymized) to validate real-world patterns. We separate cold-cache (first-token) and warm-cache (KV/prefix cached) measurements.

I attached a short executive summary and a proposed flighting workbook that maps your asks to test cases. Dev will follow up with concrete numbers and methodology. Proposed next step: 30–45 minute workshop next Tue to align on the exact dataset and SLA targets.

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RFI: performance details needed for inference platform evaluation

Alex — digging in with concrete detail below. I'll summarize methodology first and then paste the key tables. Happy to run additional configs you specify.

Methodology (short):
- Hardware baseline: tests run on a single 8x A100-equivalent NVLink pool (same GPU family across nodes). For cluster test, we used a 2-node active-active pool (8x A100 each) behind our smart router.
- Models: open-checkpoint LLM v2.1 (quantization-aware run), and a bumped embeddings model for batch tests.
- Traffic: we ran three traffic shapes: steady-state ramp to target QPS (3000s), short bursts (10s spikes at 3x baseline), and diurnal-synth (sinusoidal over 1hr). For replay tests we used anonymized traces with p95 request sizes ~220 tokens and p99 ~980.
- Cache: cold first-token measured by clearing KV cache per virtual session; warm measured after typical conversational prefixes are cached.
- Metrics: per-request latency (first-token and full-response), tokens/sec, median/95/99 tail latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth.

Summary results (representative):
- Short chat (avg 40 tokens resp): single 8x pool: p50=38ms, p95=102ms, p99=235ms. 2-node cluster (active-active): p50=36ms, p95=95ms, p99=210ms. Throughput at 95ms p95 target: ~1450 rps (concurrent short-chat sessions) on single 8x.
- Long-context chat (avg 800 tokens resp): single 8x pool: p50=420ms, p95=980ms, p99=1.9s. 2-node cluster: p50=390ms, p95=860ms, p99=1.6s. Tokens/sec sustained at 200 tokens/context: ~18k tokens/sec single 8x.
- Embeddings batch (1000 inputs, 768-d): single 8x qps: batch throughput ~230 batches/sec (1000 each) when using batched kernel path; end-to-end latency per batch p95=310ms.

Scaling behavior: latency remains near-linear with QPS until queueing thresholds. For short-chat we observe graceful degradation — up to 2x baseline QPS latency increases p95 by ~1.6x; beyond 3x queueing latency grows non-linearly and we recommend autoscale or traffic shaping. For long-context workloads, memory pressure is the primary limiter; when active session count increases, we hit GPU memory oversubscription and fall back to model-sharding or reduced batch sizes which increases latency.

Autoscaling and controls: Redwood supports two autoscale modes: predictive (based on request trend + warm-up) and reactive (based on queue depth and latency SLO). We also expose per-route batching knobs (max_batch_size, max_batch_latency_ms), quantization profile toggles, and prefix caching TTL. Recommended defaults for your workload are in the attached load-script-v2.yaml and the flight workbook.

Caveats / notes:
- Our numbers are representative from our in-house runs; customer-specific model weights or extremely long contexts (>2k tokens) can shift p99 substantially.
- Quantized runs (4-bit) reduce GPU memory and improve throughput but may add ~3-6% generation variance depending on model family.

If helpful, we can run a replay of a sanitized Novacorp trace (you provide) under the two cluster profiles and share a side-by-side report.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Dev — this is extremely helpful. Quick clarifications:

- For the long-context numbers, can you confirm whether those p99s are measured with KV prefix caching enabled, or are they pure model decode latencies (no caching)?
- For the embeddings batch, is that using FP16 kernels or a quantized kernel path?
- Can you add a run that shows behavior when one node is in maintenance (degraded 50% capacity) to validate graceful degradation and failover?

If you can add those three points to the workbook we can forward to procurement. Also interested in scheduling the workshop — Tue the 28th PST works for our team.

Alex

Alex — quick additions to address your clarifications and next steps.

- Long-context p99 above was reported with prefix KV caching enabled for sessions where prefixes repeated (warm-cache). We've added a cold-cache baseline (clearing KV) to the workbook: cold-cache p99 for long-context single 8x = 2.6s. Warm-cache p99 = 1.9s as reported.
- Embeddings batch runs referenced above used FP16 kernels; we also ran an int8-quantized batched-path that improved throughput by ~18% with p95 latency trade-off of ~+40ms per batch. Details in load-script-v2.yaml (attached).
- We ran a maintenance degrade test: one-node degraded to 50% capacity (simulated by CPU/GPU thermals + scheduling throttles). Short-chat p95 rose from 102ms to 230ms; long-context p95 rose from 980ms to 1.45s. Cluster failover preserved correctness and we documented transient queueing spikes — see tab "maintenance-sim" in the workbook.

Next steps: 1) I can run a sanitized replay if Novacorp shares a sample trace (we can NDAs as needed). 2) Workshop on Tue 28th PST booked — please confirm attendee list and primary SLO target (latency p95 target or cost per token target). I'll include a short lab walkthrough and we'll run a short replay live.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
